1: Congruent shapes match exactly, while similar shapes match in angle and proportion. Similar shapes differ only by a scale factor.
2: A scale factor is the ratio of a pair of corresponding lengths. Once you have it, every other length in the shape follows by multiplication.
3: Area is two-dimensional, so a length scale factor k gives k² for area. Volume is three-dimensional, so it gives k³, which is why doubling the sides multiplies the volume by eight.
4: A mirror line splits a shape into two identical halves, so each point on one side has a matching point on the other. Counting the mirror lines gives the number of symmetries.
5: The order of rotational symmetry counts how many times a shape fits onto itself in one full turn. A shape with no rotation fit has order 1.
